correctness.rationale: Pawlowski Theorem 6.3 makes Medvedev validity Pi^0_1-complete under computable many-one reductions. Xiao Theorem 6.1 supplies an explicit computable formula C(phi), with fresh p,q, preserving membership Med iff Cheq. The composite is Cheq-hardness. Cheq nonvalidity is r.e. by exhaustive persistent valuation and world enumeration on the uniformly finite V_n. By the defining Godel translation Cheq iff each companion on translated formulas; Xiao identifies L_infty with finite A_n and S4.FPFA with effective finite thickenings of A_n. Enumerating finite preorders whose cluster quotients match some A_n semidecides modal nonvalidity. Hence all three are Pi^0_1-complete, with no unsupported decidability or finite-time bound.
correctness.risk: The finite-frame upper bound requires effective *complete* finite semantics, not mere finite-model property; Xiao supplies the specific classes. No finite experiment proves the complexity claim.

value.rationale: Exact arithmetical complexity is a meaningful invariant in logic, but here it arises by direct composition of the published Medvedev hardness theorem, the published Cheq reduction, and standard effective finite-model enumeration; the modal extensions use definitional translations and available frame tables. No new reduction mechanism, structural obstruction, or motivated nontrivial comparison remains. Repackaging these established pieces as the stated three-tuple is a routine corollary rather than an independently worthwhile mathematical gap.
